topic.title: Garbage collectors — G1, ZGC, Shenandoah
topic.concept: GC reclaims unreachable objects; the core trade-off is throughput vs latency, and collector choice follows the latency SLO and heap size.
points: G1 (default since Java 9): region-based, targets pause via -XX:MaxGCPauseMillis (default 200ms).
ZGC: sub-ms pauses regardless of heap size (colored pointers + load barriers) — latency-sensitive APIs.
Shenandoah: concurrent compaction like ZGC, available in OpenJDK builds where ZGC isn't.
Selection rule: P99 < 10ms or 100GB+ heap → ZGC; balanced throughput → G1.
Know the OOM flavors: heap space, Metaspace, GC overhead limit exceeded, direct buffer memory.
topic.angle: '50ms P99 SLO, 16GB heap — which GC and why?' Strong answers name ZGC, cite pause-time mechanics, and mention what they'd measure (-Xlog:gc*, allocation rate) before switching.
